text:
Anna: Hey @matt @ravi — PTAL, pushed a small fix for a header-casing mismatch that made our router treat `X-Client-Id` and `x-client-id` differently. Tests pass locally but want a quick smoke before squashing.

Matt: On it. Can you paste the minimal repro you saw?

Anna: Repro steps:
```
# observed on local dev
curl -H 'X-Client-Id: abc' http://localhost:8080/api/route  # -> 403
curl -H 'x-client-id: abc' http://localhost:8080/api/route  # -> 200
```
I changed the middleware to normalize to lower-case and added a unit test that asserts both headers map to the same principal.

Ravi: Quick question: why choose lowercase normalize vs using net/http `CanonicalHeaderKey`? That one is standard.

Anna: I tried `CanonicalHeaderKey`, but it canonicalizes to Title-Case (e.g., `X-Client-Id`) which then mismatched a downstream header-check that expects lower case keys in our header map. I left a comment in the code explaining this and kept lower-case normalization to minimize churn.

Matt: Code looks straightforward. Two tiny nits inline (naming and a comment), will push a fixup if you don't mind.

Anna: Go ahead — rebased onto latest main and pushed earlier to avoid the go.mod conflict.

ci-bot: Build started. Running unit + integration suites.

Lisa: Quick FYI from QA — they'd like a 30m canary window after merge to run their dev traffic script.

Ravi: No perf regressions expected; the normalize step adds a small allocation per request but it's negligible. If concerned we can gate behind a feature flag.

ci-bot: CI passed — unit: 78/78, integration: 12/12.

Matt: LGTM from me. @release-ops can we schedule a small canary tomorrow 09:00 PT? Keep it on a single shard.

release-ops: Scheduled — 09:00 PT canary, 30m, single shard. Rollback playbook attached to the runbook.

Anna: Thanks everyone — merging after squashing commits. PTAL if anything else pops up.

Matt: :thumbsup:

Ravi: Nice catch, Anna!
